task_definition.task_name: DAS Wavefield Decomposition using FK Filtering

task_description.overview: Separate seismic wavefield into components based on apparent velocity using 2D Fourier (FK) domain filtering.
steps: Load the raw DAS waveform matrix and associated metadata (channel spacing and sampling rate).
Preprocess the data by removing spikes and bad channels.
Apply 2D FFT to transform the data into frequency–wavenumber (FK) domain.
Design a velocity‐based filter window with lower and upper apparent velocity bounds (vmin).
Multiply the FK spectrum by the taper window (e.g., Tukey) and isolate desired velocity bands.
Perform inverse 2D FFT to obtain separated time–distance wavefields for seismic and traffic signals.

task_definition.agent_prompt: Perform FK filtering on the DAS waveform data ({waveform_data_path}) with channel spacing of 8 m and sampling rate of 250 Hz. Perform the `spike_removal` and `channel_checking(use=True)` on the loaded daspy section object. Then, perform fk_filter(vmin=vmin_bounds, mode='decompose') to decompose the wavefield into two separated wavefields: one containing seismic waves and the other containing traffic signals. Finally, plot a figure (3x2) to show the waveform (original waveform, the separated seismic component, the separated traffic component) and their corresponding FK spectrum. Note: try to use daspy package to load, process and visualize the data. 2) Save the decomposed earthquake data to {decomposed_earthquake_data} and the decomposed traffic data to {decomposed_traffic_data} and save the plot to {decomposed_plot}.
